A spoon

Hide eyes
Lie down

A scarf
A coat
Snow boots

Sandals
Goggles
A fan

A pencil
A balloon

Hot milk

Snow
Stars
Lightning

payload.snippet: Heavy rain outside. What to wear?
options: A raincoat
A swimsuit
A sun hat
Light shoes

payload.snippet: Frost on the grass. How does it feel?

Very hot
Warm
Soft
payload.explanation: Frost is icy cold.

payload.snippet: A strong gust blows. Hold on to what?
options: The fence
A cloud
The sky
A puddle

payload.snippet: Sun is too hot outside. Best place?
options: In the shade
On hot sand
On a roof
By a fire
payload.explanation: Shade cools you fast.

payload.snippet: Soft drizzle falls. What helps stay dry?
options: A hood
A bib
A bell
A bow
payload.explanation: Hoods cover your hair.

payload.snippet: Wind howls loud at night. Close what?
options: The window
Your eyes
The lamp
The book
payload.explanation: Closed windows block wind.

payload.snippet: Sky is grey all day. What might happen?
options: It might rain
Stars come out
Snow only inside
Sun melts toys
payload.explanation: Grey skies often rain.

payload.snippet: After a snowfall. What to build?
options: A snowman
A sandcastle
A kite
A puddle
payload.explanation: Snow makes great snowmen.

payload.snippet: Rain pours down. Best place to play?
options: Inside the house
On wet grass
On a roof
In a puddle pile
payload.explanation: Indoors stays dry and fun.

payload.snippet: Dark clouds gather quickly while everyone walks home from the park.
options: Head home quickly
Stop to count clouds
Sit on a wet bench
Climb a tall tree
payload.explanation: Quick walks beat the rain.

payload.snippet: A strong wind picks up and leaves swirl through the playground.
options: Hold the hat tight
Chase every leaf
Climb the tallest slide
Shout at the wind to stop
payload.explanation: Holding the hat keeps it safe.

payload.snippet: Snow piles up by the front door making it hard to open.
options: Shovel a clear path
Push the door harder
Wait for spring
Hide the snow indoors
payload.explanation: Shovelling makes a safe path.

payload.snippet: The summer sun feels very hot during the long bike ride.
options: Drink cool water often
Take off the helmet
Ride faster to cool down
Sit on the hot tarmac
payload.explanation: Water cools your body down.

payload.snippet: Fog rolls in just before crossing the street to school.
options: Wait for the fog to lift
Run across without looking
Close your eyes and walk
Crawl across the road
payload.explanation: Slow + careful keeps you safe.

payload.snippet: Big rain puddles cover the whole path to the school gate.
options: Walk around the puddles
Splash through them in shoes
Sit in the deepest one
Pick the puddles up
payload.explanation: Walking around keeps shoes dry.

payload.snippet: A loud thunderclap shakes the windows while playing outside.
options: Go indoors right away
Shelter under a tree
Climb on the swing set
Wave at the sky
payload.explanation: Inside is safer than under trees.

payload.snippet: The sky turns very dark in the middle of the afternoon.
options: Pack up and head inside
Open all the windows
Set up a picnic outside
Take a long bath outdoors
payload.explanation: Dark skies often mean a storm.

payload.snippet: A heatwave is forecast for the whole afternoon at the park.
options: Wear a hat and sunscreen
Wear a heavy coat
Skip drinking water all day
Run all afternoon in jeans
payload.explanation: Hats and sunscreen block sun rays.

payload.snippet: Ice covers the steps outside the house overnight.
options: Hold the rail carefully
Run down the steps fast
Slide down on a tray
Hop down both feet at once
payload.explanation: Holding the rail prevents falls.

payload.snippet: After a long rain a beautiful rainbow appears in the sky.
options: Look up and enjoy it
Try to grab the rainbow
Cover your eyes from it
Throw a ball at it
payload.explanation: Rainbows are nice to admire.

payload.snippet: A blizzard is starting just as the family arrives at the park.
options: Head back home now
Build a snow tower
Race down the longest hill
Take off boots in snow
payload.explanation: Heading home avoids the worst snow.

payload.snippet: Frost has frozen the bike chain stiff this morning.
options: Warm it up gently
Hit the chain with a stone
Pour hot water on the frame
Leave it broken
payload.explanation: Gentle warming protects metal.

payload.snippet: The wind is strong enough to wobble the bicycle on the lane.
options: Slow down and steer steady
Lift both hands off the bars
Speed up to fight the gust
Stand on the seat
payload.explanation: Steady steering beats a gust.

payload.snippet: Strong sun shines down through the car window for hours.
options: Use the window shade
Touch the hot seat metal
Open the sunroof wide
Sit on the dashboard
payload.explanation: Shades block the hot rays.

payload.snippet: Light drizzle starts during the soccer practice on the field.
options: Keep playing carefully
Stop and lie on the wet grass
Throw the ball at clouds
Take shoes off in puddles
payload.explanation: Light rain is fine to play in.

payload.snippet: The wind howls loudly outside the bedroom window at night.
options: Close the window tight
Open every window
Leave the curtains flapping
Sleep with feet outside
payload.explanation: Closed windows keep the wind out.

payload.snippet: A cloudy sky has hidden the sun all morning at the picnic.
options: Pack a light jacket
Wear only swimwear
Put sunscreen on toes only
Stand still until it clears
payload.explanation: Jackets help when sun is hidden.

payload.snippet: Heavy snowfall buried the small garden swing overnight.
options: Brush the snow off carefully
Yank the swing chain hard
Sit on the snow pile
Push the swing into the snow
payload.explanation: Gentle brushing protects the swing.

payload.snippet: A sudden downpour soaks the picnic blanket on the grass.
options: Move under a shelter
Stand in the rain shouting
Eat under a soaked blanket
Roll on the wet blanket
payload.explanation: Shelter keeps food and people dry.

payload.snippet: A thunderstorm rolls in just as the family finishes setting up the tent for the camping trip.
options: Pack the food inside the tent first
Light a campfire to scare the storm
Stay outside to enjoy the thunder up close
Open the tent flaps for ventilation
payload.explanation: Securing food keeps it dry through the storm.

payload.snippet: Strong winds bend the trees during the school's afternoon outdoor sports practice.
options: Move the equipment to the indoor gym
Continue practice on the open field
Tie all the kids to a tree
Use the wind to throw the ball further
payload.explanation: Indoor sports stay safe in high winds.

payload.snippet: A heatwave is announced and the city issues a public health warning for the weekend.
options: Stay indoors during the hottest hours
Plan a noon-time soccer tournament
Wear a winter coat all day
Skip drinking water to save trips
payload.explanation: Avoiding peak heat protects health.

payload.snippet: Heavy snow has been falling for hours and the school bus has not arrived at the stop.
options: Walk back home and call the school
Stand and wait until midnight
Try to push a car through the snow
Build a fort in the snow drift
payload.explanation: Returning safely + calling is the smart plan.

payload.snippet: A foggy morning has made it nearly impossible to see across the playground.
options: Use bright clothes and stay together
Race each other in the fog
Climb the highest jungle gym
Hide and ask friends to find you
payload.explanation: Bright clothes + groups stay visible.

payload.snippet: Hailstones the size of marbles start pounding the car windshield on the highway.
options: Pull over carefully under cover
Drive faster to escape the hail
Roll the windows down for fresh air
Get out to collect the hail
payload.explanation: Pulling over protects you and the car.

payload.snippet: The forecast predicts a rare tornado warning for the small town this afternoon.
options: Move to the basement immediately
Watch the sky from the upstairs window
Hold an umbrella against the tornado
Set up a kite to ride the wind
payload.explanation: Basements are the safest spots in tornadoes.

payload.snippet: After a week of rain the river behind the house has risen close to the back garden fence.
options: Tell the parents about the rising water
Walk into the river to measure depth
Build a sandcastle by the water
Ignore it and keep playing
payload.explanation: Adults need to know about flood risk.

payload.snippet: The wind chill warning says exposed skin will freeze within ten minutes outside.
options: Cover every patch of skin warmly
Wear shorts to feel the wind
Sit on the ice to feel the cold
Skip socks to save on laundry
payload.explanation: Covered skin avoids quick freezing.

payload.snippet: A sudden cloudburst floods the road just as everyone is leaving the cinema.
options: Wait under the cinema awning
Run barefoot through the flood
Try to swim through the puddles
Carry friends across one by one
payload.explanation: Awnings shelter you until the rain eases.

payload.snippet: Lightning flashes very close while everyone is swimming in the open-air pool.
options: Get everyone out of the pool quickly
Stay in to watch the show
Stand on the diving board for the view
Float on a metal raft
payload.explanation: Water + metal + lightning is dangerous.

payload.snippet: A long heatwave has dried the school garden and the plants look very wilted.
options: Water plants in the early morning
Pour boiling water on the plants
Cover plants with thick black plastic
Stop watering to test how strong they are
payload.explanation: Morning water reaches roots before it evaporates.

payload.snippet: A sudden blizzard turns the highway into a sheet of white in seconds.
options: Slow down and turn hazard lights on
Speed up to get through quickly
Stop and get out to look around
Turn the headlights off to see snow better
payload.explanation: Slow speeds + hazards keep cars visible.

payload.snippet: Heavy rain has caused water to leak through the ceiling of the bedroom.
options: Place a bucket and tell an adult
Sleep under the leak to feel it
Cover the leak with a pillow
Climb on the roof to fix it alone
payload.explanation: Buckets + adult help solve leaks safely.

payload.snippet: The sun is shining very bright on the snow during a long winter hike.
options: Wear sunglasses to protect eyes
Stare at the snow without protection
Walk with eyes shut tight
Tilt the head back to enjoy the glare
payload.explanation: Snow reflects strong UV — sunglasses help.

payload.snippet: A heavy fog has rolled into the harbour and the small boat is still at sea.
options: Use the foghorn to signal others
Speed up to leave the fog faster
Turn off all the lights to save power
Stand on the bow to spot the shore
payload.explanation: Foghorns help others hear you near.

payload.snippet: A flood warning has been broadcast and the river road is starting to fill with water.
options: Take the higher road home
Drive through the deepest part
Park the car right in the river
Wait by the bank to watch the flood
payload.explanation: Higher roads stay above flood water.

payload.snippet: The rainy season has begun and water is starting to pool around the front steps.
options: Dig a small drain to redirect it
Let the water flood the entrance
Add a big rug on top of the puddle
Block the drain with leaves
payload.explanation: Drains move water away from the door.

payload.snippet: A morning frost has made the grass stiff and crunchy under the boots.
options: Walk carefully on the path
Run barefoot to feel the cold
Stomp to break every blade
Spray hot water on the lawn
payload.explanation: Careful walking protects feet and the grass.

payload.snippet: A summer thunderstorm rolls in during the family picnic at the lakeside park.
options: Pack up and head to the car
Stand by the lake to feel the rain
Hold a metal pole during the storm
Swim out into the lake
payload.explanation: Cars are safer than open lakeshores.

payload.snippet: A rare ice storm has coated the trees, power lines, and walkways near the house with a thick layer of clear, heavy ice overnight.
options: Stay indoors and warn the family about falling branches
Climb a tree to break off the icicles
Use a torch to melt all the ice off the wires
Take a brisk run through the icy garden
payload.explanation: Ice-laden branches and lines fall without warning, so staying inside is safest.

payload.snippet: A long heatwave has made the local tap water taste strange and the doctor has warned everyone to drink only bottled water for the day.
options: Use only sealed bottled water for the day
Boil the tap water briefly and gulp it down
Skip drinking entirely to be safe
Mix tap water with juice to mask the taste
payload.explanation: Sealed bottles are the only sure-safe option until water is cleared.

payload.snippet: A snowstorm has knocked the power out and the heating is off across the whole neighbourhood for the rest of the evening.
options: Gather in one warm room with blankets
Open every door so the cold balances out
Light a barbecue grill indoors for heat
Take a long shower for warmth
payload.explanation: One warm shared room conserves body heat safely.

payload.snippet: A flash flood warning has been issued and the small creek behind the school has overflowed its banks during the lunchtime break.
options: Move to a higher classroom on the top floor
Wade into the creek to rescue the lunchboxes
Take photos right at the edge of the water
Race the rising water on bikes
payload.explanation: Higher floors keep students above the rising flood waters.

payload.snippet: A sandstorm has been forecast for the desert town and visibility is dropping quickly during the family road trip.
options: Pull off the road and wait it out safely
Drive faster to outrun the sandstorm
Stop the car and step out to take photos
Roll down all windows for fresh air
payload.explanation: Stopping safely in the storm beats driving blind through sand.

payload.snippet: A sudden change in pressure means a thunderstorm is rolling toward the soccer tournament that just kicked off on the open pitch.
options: Call the referee to pause the match
Continue the game and ignore the storm
Put on metal cleats to grip the wet grass
Hold a metal pole as a flag
payload.explanation: Pausing the match keeps players off open ground when lightning is near.

payload.snippet: A heat dome has settled over the city and the apartment block elevator has stopped working because of a power cut.
options: Take the stairs slowly with water in hand
Sprint up all the stairs as fast as possible
Wait alone in the dark hallway forever
Open the elevator doors and climb the shaft
payload.explanation: Slow climbs with hydration prevent heat exhaustion.

payload.snippet: A whiteout is making it impossible to see anything beyond an arm's length during the cross-country ski trip in the mountains.
options: Stop, stay together, and wait for visibility
Spread out to find the path faster
Try to ski downhill at full speed
Bury the gear and walk back
payload.explanation: Staying put + together until the whiteout passes is the safer call.

payload.snippet: A monsoon downpour has filled the basement with several centimetres of water during a long, wet weekend.
options: Switch off electricity and call for help
Wade in to grab a hairdryer
Plug in extra fans to dry the floor
Walk barefoot across the wet floor
payload.explanation: Power must be off before anyone enters water near electrical sockets.

payload.snippet: A sudden hailstorm has shattered one of the greenhouse panels just as the new seedlings were being planted for the season.
options: Cover the seedlings with a sheet
Pick up the broken glass barehanded
Run through the broken pane shoeless
Open the rest of the panels too
payload.explanation: Covering protects fragile seedlings until repairs can happen safely.

payload.snippet: A heat advisory warns that pavement temperatures will be hot enough to burn skin during the planned afternoon dog walk in the park.
options: Walk the dog at sunrise instead
Carry the dog across the hot pavement
Put boots on the dog and walk at noon
Let the dog walk barefoot to toughen up
payload.explanation: Cool sunrise pavement protects paw pads from burns.

payload.snippet: A windstorm has knocked over the school playground tree and one of the branches has fallen across the main gate.
options: Use the side gate and tell a teacher
Climb over the fallen branch
Try to lift the branch alone
Saw the branch with a kitchen knife
payload.explanation: Side gates are safe + adults handle the fallen branch.

payload.snippet: A blizzard warning has been issued and the school principal has asked everyone to make sure they have a winter emergency kit ready in the lockers.
options: Stock the locker with snacks, water, and a torch
Pack only summer clothes in the locker
Skip the kit because winter passes fast
Fill the locker with melted snow
payload.explanation: Snacks, water, and a torch cover the basics for a snow emergency.

payload.snippet: A heat wave has caused several outdoor sports practices in the league to be moved to the early morning slot for the rest of the month.
options: Set the alarm earlier and pack water
Skip practice for a month
Practice at noon to prove toughness
Wear thick wool gear during practice
payload.explanation: Early alarms + water keep heat-shifted practice safe.

payload.snippet: A sudden frost has been forecast overnight and the citrus trees in the garden are full of fruit that has not yet been picked.
options: Cover the trees with frost cloth
Spray the trees with cold water
Cut down the trees to save the fruit
Leave the fruit and hope for the best
payload.explanation: Frost cloth traps just enough warmth to protect the fruit.

payload.snippet: A long drought has lowered the river to a trickle and the town council is asking everyone to reduce water use by half for the coming weeks.
options: Take shorter showers and skip baths
Wash the car every single day
Leave the garden hose running all night
Refuse to follow the council request
payload.explanation: Short showers + skipping baths halve typical home water use.

payload.snippet: A windy afternoon has carried sparks from a nearby bonfire toward the dry grass at the back of the camping site.
options: Douse the fire with water immediately
Add more dry wood for fun
Move the fire closer to the dry grass
Cover the fire with a polyester tent
payload.explanation: Wet ash prevents sparks from reaching the dry grass.

payload.snippet: A foggy night has rolled into the coastal road and the cycle ride home is taking far longer than expected because of poor visibility.
options: Walk the bikes home with lights on
Ride twice as fast to finish sooner
Turn the lights off to save battery
Hold onto a passing car instead
payload.explanation: Slow walks + lights stay visible to passing cars.

payload.snippet: A snowstorm has been falling for the last six hours and the road outside is now buried under almost a metre of fresh snow.
options: Stay home and reschedule the trip
Drive carefully through the metre of snow
Walk all the way without warm gear
Send the dog out to break the trail
payload.explanation: Rescheduling beats driving through a buried road.

payload.snippet: A sudden tropical downpour has flooded the path between the campsite and the toilet block during the family camping holiday.
options: Wait under shelter for the rain to pass
Wade through the flooded path barefoot
Build a raft from sleeping bags
Crawl through the puddle for fun
payload.explanation: Sheltering keeps clothes and shoes dry while the rain passes.

payload.snippet: A category three hurricane is forecast to make landfall within twelve hours and the local authorities have issued an urgent evacuation notice for everyone living along the entire coastline.
options: Pack essentials and drive inland straight away
Stay on the beach to watch the waves get bigger
Tie all the patio furniture to one large tree
Open every window to balance the pressure inside the house
payload.explanation: Inland evacuation is the safest option when authorities raise a hurricane alert.

payload.snippet: A blizzard combined with a power failure has left the family stranded inside a remote mountain cabin without heating for the entire night and the temperatures are dropping rapidly.
options: Gather everyone into the warmest room with extra blankets
Light a barbecue grill on the kitchen floor for warmth
Open the door for fresh air every ten minutes
Run a small petrol generator inside the lounge
payload.explanation: Sharing one warm room with insulation conserves body heat without any carbon-monoxide risk.

payload.snippet: A heatwave has pushed temperatures to record highs and the school's air conditioning system has just failed during the longest classroom session of the week.
options: Move classes to the cool basement library
Continue lessons in full uniform with windows shut
Hand out warm drinks to balance the heat
Skip drinking water until break time
payload.explanation: The cool basement keeps everyone safe until the air conditioning is restored.

payload.snippet: A flash flood has overtaken the main road back to town just as the family minivan reaches a low river crossing and the water is already past the wheel tops.
options: Reverse carefully to higher ground and call for help
Drive faster through the rising water
Step out to push the van across the flood
Wait inside the van for the water to lower on its own
payload.explanation: Reversing to high ground avoids the danger of a stalled vehicle in moving water.

payload.snippet: A long-running drought has reduced the town reservoir to ten percent of normal levels and the mayor has issued strict water rationing rules for the next four months.
options: Capture rainwater and reuse household greywater carefully
Continue watering the lawn three times a day
Fill the swimming pool for the kids each weekend
Wash the family cars every morning
payload.explanation: Greywater reuse + rainwater capture multiply each litre while the rationing rules hold.

payload.snippet: A severe ice storm has glazed every road, bridge, and overpass in the city and the highway patrol has asked drivers to avoid any non-essential travel for the next twenty-four hours.
options: Cancel the planned weekend trip and stay home
Set off early to beat the ice
Take the highest mountain pass for better views
Borrow studded tyres at noon and drive across the city
payload.explanation: Cancelling avoids the genuine danger of black ice on every kind of roadway.

payload.snippet: A wildfire has been racing toward the edge of the small mountain town for the last two hours and a local volunteer has knocked on the door asking everyone to leave within thirty minutes.
options: Grab the go-bag and leave by the marked route
Climb to the roof to film the fire approaching
Stay behind to defend the property with a garden hose
Pack the entire library before evacuating
payload.explanation: The marked evacuation route was chosen because it stays clear of the fire's path.

payload.snippet: A monsoon that has been pouring for the entire week has saturated the hillside above the village and a landslide warning has been broadcast on the local radio station this morning.
options: Move down to the community shelter quickly
Walk up the hill to check what is happening
Build a small wall of garden stones to stop the slide
Wait in the back garden under an umbrella
payload.explanation: The shelter sits below the slide line and offers far stronger walls than a house.

payload.snippet: A sudden severe thunderstorm has caught the school group out on the open soccer pitch during the regional inter-school championship final match this evening.
options: Bring all the players into the main school building
Continue the match to crown the winner
Tell the players to lie flat on the pitch
Stand under the tallest tree as a group
payload.explanation: The main building, away from trees and water, is the safest place during close lightning.

payload.snippet: A whiteout snowstorm has reduced visibility to less than a metre during a long-distance cross-country ski expedition through the high arctic plateau region this afternoon.
options: Cluster the team together and pitch the emergency tent
Spread out fast to cover more ground
Ski downhill toward an unseen valley
Bury the skis and walk back without GPS
payload.explanation: An emergency tent + clustering keeps everyone warm and easy to find when visibility returns.

payload.snippet: A polar vortex has dropped temperatures to minus forty degrees overnight and the school has been closed but the family heating system has unexpectedly stopped working an hour ago.
options: Move to a neighbour's home and call the heating company
Light all the gas burners on the stove for heat
Open the front door to let warmer outside air in
Run a long shower to warm the bathroom
payload.explanation: Neighbours' heated homes + a professional call solve the cold safely.

payload.snippet: A heat dome has settled over the region and a public health alert warns that anyone outside for longer than fifteen minutes at midday risks heat stroke without protection.
options: Reschedule errands to the early morning hours
Take the long walk through the noon sun
Skip the sun hat to look stylish
Drink hot chocolate to balance the heat
payload.explanation: Early hours combine cooler air with a fresh body and full hydration.

payload.snippet: A series of tornado watches have been issued across the entire region and the family has just sat down to dinner in the conservatory with full glass walls all around.
options: Move dinner to the windowless central room
Stay in the glass room to watch the sky
Open the conservatory roof to vent the pressure
Set up a video camera right outside the window
payload.explanation: A windowless central room is the recommended shelter against flying debris.

payload.snippet: A storm surge from the approaching cyclone is expected to push sea water several streets inland tonight and the local council has urged residents to lift everything off the floor.
options: Lift electronics and important papers onto top shelves
Leave everything on the floor as a test
Tape the front door to keep the surge out
Open the back gate to let the water flow through
payload.explanation: Raising belongings protects against the surge's deepest expected push inland.

payload.snippet: A long drought has weakened the roots of the old oak tree behind the house and the latest forecast warns of a powerful overnight wind storm with sustained gusts of over a hundred kilometres an hour.
options: Sleep in the front bedroom away from the oak side
Sleep directly under the oak to enjoy the breeze
Tie the tree to the roof with a rope
Open every window facing the oak side
payload.explanation: The front bedroom is safe even if the weakened oak falls in the storm.

payload.snippet: A severe heatwave has buckled several stretches of the train track between the two main stations and the rail company has suspended every service for the entire weekend.
options: Reschedule the trip and book a refund online
Walk along the buckled track instead of waiting
Climb onto a parked train to wait there
Try to fix the buckled rail with a hammer
payload.explanation: Rescheduling avoids both heat danger and the legal risk of walking on tracks.

payload.snippet: A sudden derecho has produced straight-line winds powerful enough to flatten part of the city's tree canopy in less than fifteen minutes during the late afternoon commute.
options: Pull off the road into a sturdy car park
Drive faster on the open highway
Park directly under the tallest road tree
Get out of the car to take live video
payload.explanation: Sturdy car parks shelter vehicles from falling branches and rolling debris.

payload.snippet: A flood that has been rising slowly for three days has now isolated the small island village from the mainland and the regional helicopter team has just radioed an evacuation message.
options: Pack one waterproof bag and head to the helipad
Pack four large suitcases for the flight
Stay home and wave the helicopter away
Climb onto the church roof to wait
payload.explanation: One waterproof bag fits the helicopter while letting the team work fast.

payload.snippet: A long-running wildfire has produced smoke so thick across the valley that the air quality index has stayed in the hazardous range for the third consecutive day this summer.
options: Stay indoors with an air filter running
Open every window for fresh air
Go on a long bike ride through the smoke
Run a leaf blower outside to clear the smoke
payload.explanation: Indoor air + a filter cuts smoke exposure far below the hazardous outdoor level.

payload.snippet: A nor'easter has produced enormous waves on the small coastal harbour and the marine forecast has issued a small-craft advisory that lasts well into next Monday morning.
options: Keep all boats moored in the harbour
Sail straight out to ride the biggest wave
Tow the boats out one by one for fun
Anchor in the deepest open water
payload.explanation: Moored boats inside the harbour are the safer choice until the advisory clears.
